transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2027-08-19 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Priya Raman (Redwood SE); Aaron Patel, Leah Torres, Julio Reyes, Nora Kim (Hillcrest)

Auto-summary (auto): Medium confidence - kickoff / intake / ask for runbook and CIDR; action items captured.

Topics: onboarding topology, VPC & network, KMS, staging vs prod, SLA expectations, pilot metrics

--- Transcript starts ---
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone thanks for joining on time, uh this is Maya from Redwood inference, i'll kick off real quick. we've got Diego and Priya on our side, and i see Hillcrest on the line - Aaron, Leah, Julio, Nora, hey.
[00:12] Aaron Patel: Hey Maya, thanks. quick note, we might hop off a bit early for another sync, but should be fine.
[00:17] Diego Alvarez: No worries, we can prioritize the network + security item first.
[00:23] Priya Raman: Yeah i'll go over the staging topology, what we recommend for the onramp and the typical capacity profile for a 2-week pilot. some of the names i use might be shorthand — redwood private or redwood dedi, sorry sometimes i say red-wood private, that's our private deployment option.
[00:38] Leah Torres: Great. we're mainly interested in private deployment with a VPC peering to our AWS account. can you confirm if you support customer-managed KMS for key wrapping?
[00:47] Priya Raman: Yes, you can bring-your-own-KMS — we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS or cloud HSM). small caveat: for on-prem/lite setups we ask for an HSM connection plan. i will drop exact config snippets in the runbook.
[00:59] Julio Reyes: When you say "drop" is that in a doc link? we need to ensure it's stored in our Confluence not public.
[01:05] Priya Raman: Absolutely — we'll share a private runbook link to your SSO group. Diego will give you access.

[01:15] Agenda checkpoint
[01:17] Maya Chen: Quick agenda: 1) network/VPC intake 2) runtime sizing for pilot 3) security & audit logs 4) observability and cost controls 5) success criteria and next steps. sound good?
[01:25] Aaron Patel: Yep.

[02:05] Nora Kim: A couple specifics on VPC: we want to avoid NAT egress, prefer VPC peering over transit gateway. is that supported?
[02:13] Priya Raman: We support both peering and TGW. Peering is fine for small pilots. a couple notes: you'll need to allow the Redwood egress IP ranges or set up an interface endpoint for control plane. we'll include the cidr ranges in the runbook.
[02:26] Nora Kim: Can you send the CIDR list now?
[02:28] Diego Alvarez: i'll follow up with the exact list after this call, aim to include examples for interface endpoints and route table changes.

[03:00] Leah Torres: On capacity — our main workloads are interactive chat + embeddings, mixed QPS with spikes 200-400 reqs/min. what's the starting config?
[03:11] Priya Raman: For that pattern, we usually propose a small dedicated pool — 2x A10-like GPUs (or equivalent A200) sized to your latency SLO. for early pilot we can run hosted but isolated in a dedicated tenancy — but since you want private we will recommend dedicated nodes in your VPC via our private control plane.
[03:28] Aaron Patel: Are there quantization choices we should commit to up front? we've got an LLM with 8k context.
[03:35] Priya Raman: We typically recommend 8-bit quant for cost, but keep a float fallback for quality checks. we'll provide a recommendation matrix in the runbook by model family, seq len and latency target.

[04:12] Julio Reyes: Security: audit logs, retention, and RBAC. we need logs to ship to our SIEM and 365-day retention. does Redwood support forwarding audit logs?
[04:22] Diego Alvarez: Yes, audit logs can be forwarded to your S3 or event hub. retention is configurable on your side; for hosted we store only metadata by default but for private we can mirror full request logs to your bucket. note: request payloads have sensitive PII redaction options, we can enable automatic redaction or tokenization.
[04:39] Julio Reyes: Good — need that in writing for our SOC questionnaire.
[04:42] Maya Chen: We'll attach the security pack and SOC/ISO artifact in the follow-up email.

[05:20] Nora Kim: Observability — how do we get per-route latency & cost metrics?
[05:26] Priya Raman: Redwood console exposes per-token cost and route dashboards. for private we ship a telemetry agent that posts to your prometheus & grafana endpoints, or you can scrape our metrics endpoint. small warning: naming sometimes in the UI is "route" vs "endpoint" — that tripped some teams.
[05:41] Aaron Patel: Is there a way to sample requests for quality monitoring without sending raw data?
[05:46] Diego Alvarez: Yes, you can enable sampling and only forward model outputs post-redaction. we'll show the eval hooks in the runbook.

[06:30] Priya Raman: i want to walk through the staging topology real quick — two subnets, one for control plane, one for inference nodes. control plane needs a NAT or egress to our control endpoints unless you set up an interface endpoint. inference nodes can be private-only with S3 access via VPC endpoint for model artifacts.
[06:51] Leah Torres: Any special ports?
[06:54] Priya Raman: Mostly HTTPS (443) and a few health probe ports; we'll enumerate them.

[08:00] Aaron Patel: Network latency: what's the expected added latency for peering vs hosted?
[08:07] Priya Raman: Peering typically adds 1-5 ms within region; hosted may be a few ms lower but the difference is small relative to model infer times. main tradeoff is control and data residency.

[09:00] Leah Torres: Pilot success metrics: what do you recommend?
[09:05] Diego Alvarez: We usually run a 2-week pilot with these metrics: p95 latency under X ms (we'll calibrate), throughput targets met, cost per 1k tokens under agreed threshold, and no regressions on 10 canonical prompts. also we add an incident runbook.
[09:20] Leah Torres: Ok, add quality thresholds for hallucination rate as well — we'll share prompt test set.

[10:00] Maya Chen: Timeline check: runbook by Tuesday (Priya), network details by Friday (Hillcrest), first smoke tests next Monday, full pilot kickoff the week after. for dates: Priya 2027-08-23, Hillcrest network by 2027-08-21, smoke test 2027-08-30, pilot start 2027-09-06.
[10:20] Aaron Patel: That aligns.

[12:00] Cross talk and misc items
[12:05] Julio Reyes: Regarding encryption-at-rest — if we mirror logs to S3, can those be encrypted with our KMS?
[12:11] Priya Raman: Yes, we can configure S3 server-side encryption with your KMS key. note that some auto-archival flows use a service account; we'll document the minimum IAM perms.

[14:00] Nora Kim: Onboard checklist — who is the single point of contact for infra questions?
[14:05] Diego Alvarez: Diego will be your onboarding CSM and main day-to-day. Priya is SE for infra and Maya is AE for commercial & SLA questions.

[16:00] Leah Torres: Any known blockers you see from our gaps?
[16:05] Priya Raman: The only gating items are: 1) network CIDR/peering approvals 2) KMS owner + key policy 3) service account IAM perms for model artifact S3 read. those are standard.

[20:00] Aaron Patel: One more Q — what about private model hosting (we bring our model binary)?
[20:07] Priya Raman: Supported. we'll need the model format (hf, ggml, safetensors) and we will provide an ingestion job to pull into the inference nodes. mention of 'kv cache' in the docs might be spelled K V cache — that's our internal note for cache warmup.

[24:00] Leah Torres: Do you support canary rollouts?
[24:04] Diego Alvarez: Yes, rollouts, A/B and automatic fallback to a smaller model if latency SLO is breached — all available in the console. the UI label occasionally shows 'rollout policy' vs 'deployment policy' — we'll clarify names in the runbook.

[28:30] Maya Chen: Security paperwork & procurement — Julio, you asked for SOC artifacts. we'll attach the security pack and a redwood-SOC-2.pdf in email. any procurement timing constraints?
[28:45] Julio Reyes: We have a compliance window through end of September — need signatures and vendor review before then.

[34:00] Aaron Patel: Pricing question at a high level: for pilot are we expected to pay usage or is Redwood doing a trial credit?
[34:08] Maya Chen: We'll provide pilot credits for the first two weeks; any overage will be billed at a trial rate. Diego will follow up with a short pricing note.

[38:00] Priya Raman: Technical note — for embeddings workload, consider disabling KV cache for initial run to simplify validation then enable once traffic steady. sometimes teams get cache warmup skew that affects evals.

[42:00] Nora Kim: We want to run a small benchmark: 1k concurrent tokens, measure p95. can Redwood run that or we run on our side?
[42:09] Priya Raman: We can run the benchmark from staging nodes if you give peering and IAM. otherwise you can run a client-side load with the benchmark harness we'll provide.

[46:00] Action items recap
[46:05] Diego Alvarez: Recap of action items: Priya share runbook by Tue 8/23; Diego send cidr and IP ranges and deck; Hillcrest provide KMS owner + key policy by Fri 8/21; schedule first week check-in 8/26.
[46:20] Aaron Patel: Sounds good, please cc our security mailbox.

[50:00] Closing
[50:06] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone; i'll send meeting notes and links to the runbook and security pack; we'll follow up on calendar invites for the smoke test.
[50:15] Leah Torres: Appreciate it. bye.
[50:17] Julio Reyes: Thanks bye.
--- Transcript ends ---
